name: Phú Quốc International Airport
before:
The airport for Phú Quốc island in southern Vietnam, about 9 km south of the island's administrative centre, built at a cost of around 810 million dollars to open the island up to international beach tourism.

It is already being rebuilt. Sun Group took over ownership from Airports Corporation of Vietnam in November 2025 and is delivering a major expansion: an entirely new runway alongside a lengthened existing one, plus new terminals, timed for APEC in 2027. Expect construction disruption and changing facilities over the next couple of years.

Capacity started at about 2.5 million passengers a year and is designed to reach 7 million. The single runway takes aircraft up to an A350 or 747.

It opened on 2 December 2012, replacing the old Phu Quoc Airport 10 km away.
after:
The airport for Phú Quốc island in southern Vietnam, about 9 km south of the island's administrative centre. It opened in December 2012, replacing the island's old airport. Long-haul wide-bodied jets such as the Boeing 747 can already use it.

The airport is being expanded for APEC 2027, which the island will host. Airports Corporation of Vietnam handed the airport's assets to Sun Group in November 2025, and Sun Group now runs it. The works add a second runway of 3,300 metres, a new Terminal 2 and a VIP terminal, while the existing runway is to be lengthened from 3,000 to 3,500 metres. Terminal 2 is due to open in 2027. Expect construction disruption and changing facilities over the next couple of years.

claims.why: 'Rebuilt' overstates it: the operator and Tuoi Tre describe an expansion of the working airport. Replaced by 'is being expanded' (see above).

claims.claim: a major expansion: an entirely new runway, a lengthened existing one, new terminals, timed for APEC in 2027
claims.wasBefore: is delivering a major expansion: an entirely new runway alongside a lengthened existing one, plus new terminals, timed for APEC in 2027

claims.claim: capacity started at about 2.5 million and is designed to reach 7 million
claims.wasBefore: Capacity started at about 2.5 million passengers a year and is designed to reach 7 million.
claims.why: Out of date, and the current figures disagree. Tuoi Tre (November 2025) says the 2018 expansion took the terminal from 2.65 to 4 million a year; Tuoi Tre (23 September 2026, from Sun Group) says Terminal 1 has now been enlarged to 9 million a year, which no second source gives; the April 2025 masterplan aims at about 10 million a year by 2030 and 18 million by 2050 (Tuoi Tre, June 2025), while the operator says 20 million once phase 1 is finished in 2027. So no capacity figure is given.

opinion.text: Expect construction disruption and changing facilities over the next couple of years.
opinion.why: Advice carried over from the old text.
